title: Can place values show if a number divides by eleven?
description: The number four hundred sixty two is split into four hundred, sixty and two. Each part is written as a multiple of eleven plus or minus a little, then the extras and the shortfall are added up. Keeko's doubt is that adding the digits, as for nine, shows the number is not divisible by eleven.
teaching_notes: One idea: hundreds sit a little above a multiple of eleven and tens a little below, so the extras and the shortfall can cancel. Watch for students who add all the digits, as for nine, and never take the shortfall away.

source: Use the remainders of the place values to decide whether 462
video_script.why: A learner sees that each place value sits a little above or below a multiple of eleven, so the extras and the shortfall can be added to test for eleven.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number: four hundred sixty two
video_script.anchor: the number 462 split into hundreds, tens and ones, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: four hundred sixty two is not divisible by eleven
video_script.wrong_move: adds all the digits as for nine and never takes the six for the tens away
video_script.payoff_line: Four hundred sixty two is divisible by eleven.

final_answer.spoken: four hundred sixty two is divisible by eleven

maths_rules: 11 × 36 = 396 and 396 + 4 = 400, so 400 is 4 more than a multiple of 11
11 × 6 = 66 and 66 − 6 = 60, so 60 is 6 less than a multiple of 11
2 = 0 + 2, so 2 is 2 more than the multiple 0
video_script.design: One idea: extras and shortfalls of place values cancel for eleven. Assumes place value and multiples. The three parts of the number stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: title card Divisibility by 11; the number 462 written large, with the question: is 462 divisible by 11?

marks.scene: the title card arrives and 462 is written large
marks.ask: the words divisible by 11? appear under 462

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the number four hundred sixty two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book wants us to use place values to decide something about it.
Is four hundred sixty two divisible by eleven?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.
<bookmark mark='split'/>A number splits by place value, here into four hundred, sixty and two.
Divisible by eleven means eleven goes in exactly, with nothing left over.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten is one less than eleven, so each ten sits a little below a multiple of eleven.
<bookmark mark='hundred'/>A hundred is one more than ninety nine, which is eleven times nine.

marks.given: the number and its three parts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number is four hundred sixty two, which is four hundred, sixty and two.

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find whether eleven divides four hundred sixty two exactly.

beats.on_screen: 400 = 396 + 4, and 396 = 11 × 36, so 400 is 4 more than a multiple of 11

marks.extra: 400 = 396 + 4 is written and the 4 is tagged extra

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, write four hundred using a multiple of eleven. Eleven times thirty six is three hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='extra'/>Four hundred is three hundred ninety six plus four. That makes four hundred four more than a multiple of eleven.

beats.on_screen: 60 = 66 − 6, and 66 = 11 × 6, so 60 is 6 less than a multiple of 11

marks.short: 60 = 66 − 6 is written and the 6 is tagged short

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, write sixty using a multiple of eleven. Eleven times six is sixty six.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Sixty is sixty six take away six. That makes sixty six less than a multiple of eleven.

marks.two: 2 = 0 + 2 is written and the 2 is tagged extra
marks.cancel: 4 + 2 − 6 = 0 is written, the extras and the short cancel

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, two is two more than zero, which is a multiple of eleven.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>Add the extras, four and two. Then take away the six that is short.
Four plus two take away six leaves nothing over.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Four hundred sixty two is divisible by eleven.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Eleven times forty two makes four hundred sixty two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number 462
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 4 + 6 + 2 = 12, not 11; the 6 on the tens is tagged short; the bubble is struck through

marks.short: the tag minus 6 on the sixty glows
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 4 + 2 − 6 = 0 returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four hundred sixty two is not divisible by eleven. Four plus six plus two is twelve, says Keeko.
<bookmark mark='short'/>That adds the digits, as we do for nine. But the six tens are short of a multiple of eleven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A shortfall is taken away, not added. Then the extras and the shortfall cancel.
